scope: Vision R2 outer TLS record-boundary correction after exact f3ce257f macOS and Windows interop failures; local tests only.
source_identity_scope: The local checkout base remains 271ed3f5d2abe185a7b3308dd77f00b904bc58be. The frozen file hashes identify the tested modifications; this document does not claim a new commit or exact-SHA CI result.
implementation: Explicit TlsRecordIo reads at most the current TLS header or ciphertext body and retains only a five-byte header plus counters; TLS authentication and close_notify validation remain with rustls.
Explicit PlaintextChunks consumes one authenticated plaintext chunk per read so command 2 is delivered to Vision before tokio-rustls can read a subsequent raw inner-TLS record.
The synthetic vision-client outer TLS path uses both adapters. Default product secure transport and inner TLS behavior are unchanged.
DirectRequested is still rejected with PermissionDenied. This change does not enable DirectReady, raw socket extraction, or product outbound support.

properties: A deterministic real TLS peer supplies an authenticated command-2 record followed immediately by an actual ciphertext record from an unrelated TLS session. The original batching path reproduces InvalidData and a bad-record-MAC alert.

The four ciphertext/plaintext adapter combinations demonstrate that both boundaries are required: ciphertext limiting alone can still consume raw bytes and emit an alert during a second plaintext fill.
Both adapters preserve PermissionDenied and DirectRequested, expose zero application bytes, leave the complete raw suffix unread, and drop the transport owner exactly once.
A tampered authenticated command-2 record remains InvalidData; it cannot become a DirectRequested refusal.
Authenticated close_notify succeeds; bare TCP EOF and partial close-record header/body remain UnexpectedEof.
A cancelled read preserves a partial header, upload half-close still permits downlink, and an oversized record is rejected after its five-byte header without reading its body.
